name: sardine cream cheese spread
instructions:
The best way I've found to eat sardines. A creamy raw spread built on cream cheese + mashed sardines + apple-cider-vinegar-macerated onion + finely-crushed aromatics. From Spring Council / Mama Dip (southern US cooking).

Serves 4-6 as a spread. ~15 min prep + 15 min macerate.

=== INGREDIENTS ===

- 1 pack (8 oz) cream cheese, softened
- 1 can sardines (drained — NO tomato-based sardines; olive-oil or lemon-packed is fine; see notes)
- 3 tsp apple cider vinegar
- 1/2 red onion, finely diced
- 1/2 to 1 clove garlic, minced or grated
- fennel seeds, to taste (~1/2 tsp, crushed)
- raisins, to taste (~1-2 tbsp, roughly chopped)
- salt and black pepper (adjust — sardines are already salty)

=== PROCEDURE ===

1. DRAIN THE SARDINES. Choose plain oil-packed or lemon-packed cans; NO tomato-based sardines (see notes). Add the drained sardines to a small cup or ramekin.

2. MASH THE SARDINES WITH VINEGAR: pour the 3 tsp apple cider vinegar over the sardines. Mash with a fork until the sardines break down into a rough paste. Let sit 15 minutes — the vinegar macerate mellows the sardine funk and starts breaking down the flesh.

3. COMBINE IN A BOWL: transfer the vinegar-macerated sardines to a mixing bowl. Add the softened cream cheese, finely diced red onion, garlic, crushed fennel seeds, and chopped raisins. Mix with a fork until well-integrated but still slightly rustic (don't over-blend — some texture is good).

4. TASTE + SEASON: adjust salt (careful — sardines carry a lot of salt already) and black pepper. If it needs more brightness, another splash of vinegar or a squeeze of lemon.

5. SERVE: on crackers, toast, cucumber rounds, or bread. Also good as a sandwich filling.
notes:
The best way I've found to eat sardines. From Spring Council / Mama Dip (southern US cooking tradition). The vinegar-macerate step is what makes it work — sardines straight into cream cheese would read too fishy-funky, but the acid mellows the sardines while the cream cheese carries the fat and roundness.

=== VINEGAR MACERATE IS LOAD-BEARING ===

Mash the sardines with the 3 tsp apple cider vinegar first, then let sit 15 minutes before combining with the cream cheese. The acid does two things:
1. MELLOWS THE SARDINE FUNK — raw sardines can read aggressively fishy in a raw preparation; the vinegar tames that.
2. BREAKS DOWN THE FLESH — the flakes soften and mash easier into a smoother spread.

Skip the macerate and the spread reads coarser and fishier.

=== DRAINED SARDINES — NO TOMATO, LEMON OK ===

Use sardines packed in olive oil, water, or lemon — plain enough that the cream cheese + vinegar can lead. NO tomato-based sardines — the tomato character would clash with the cream cheese base and pull the spread into an entirely different flavor register. If you only have tomato-packed, drain and rinse them thoroughly first, but the plain versions are easier.

LEMON-PACKED WORKS FINE: some brands (King Oscar, Wild Planet lemon) come with a bit of lemon in the oil. That character folds cleanly into this spread — it's basically a preview of the vinegar/citrus acid the recipe wants anyway.

=== SOFTENED CREAM CHEESE — TAKE IT OUT AHEAD ===

Cream cheese needs to be at room temperature (or close) to mix cleanly. Cold cream cheese from the fridge doesn't fold into the other ingredients evenly and you'll get lumps. Take it out at least 30 min before starting, or 15-20 sec in the microwave (don't melt it, just soften).

=== FENNEL SEEDS + RAISINS — SICILIAN-ADJACENT FLAVOR REGISTER ===

Fennel seeds + raisins is a real sicilian pairing (shows up in pasta con le sarde and sicilian sardine dishes). Crushed fennel seeds add an anise-warm note that pairs with sardines; raisins add small sweet pops that balance the salt + brine. Both to taste — don't overdo either.

=== RED ONION MACERATE (COULD ALSO BE PRE-MACERATED WITH THE SARDINES) ===

Red onion goes in finely diced. Optional refinement: dice the red onion FIRST and add it to the sardines + vinegar for the 15-min macerate too — the vinegar tames the raw onion bite at the same time it works on the sardines. Not required (the small amount of onion is fine raw) but a nice bonus if you're willing to plan ahead.

=== SERVING ===

On crackers, toast points, cucumber rounds, or bread. Also good as a sandwich filling. Pairs well with a crisp cold beverage — the spread is rich and needs something to cut through it.

=== WHY SARDINES DON'T FIT IN [[tuna-mac]] ===

Sardines were previously listed as a valid protein slot in [[tuna-mac]] alongside tuna. Walked back — sardines are too salty/savory for that dish (a baked mac and cheese with a mild dairy-forward base doesn't want the sardine intensity). Reach for this spread instead as the go-to sardine application in the cookbook.

=== SIBLING RECIPES ===

- [[sardine-parsley-pasta]]: the other sardine recipe — sicilian-adjacent pasta with sardines + parsley + fennel + lemon + pine nut breadcrumbs. Different format (pasta, hot) but same core sardine + fennel + acid flavor register.
- [[tuna-mac]]: the tuna baked-mac dish. Sardines don't fit there (see note above); tuna is the canned-fish for that recipe.
